title: FTSE Russell Q3 2026 quarterly IPO review takes effect at the open — recent IPOs enter the Russell US indexes, implemented after the 2026-09-18 close
source: EST: owner-published, read direct this session. FTSE Russell, "Frequently Asked Questions -- Russell US Equity Indexes", July 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents PDF, ftse-faq-document-russell-us-equity-2026.pdf, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, 19 content streams inflated and text-extracted in-session 2026-09-06). Its dated schedule table's "Quarterly IPO September 2026" column gives, verbatim: IPO Review Period "1 May 2026 to 31 July 2026", IPO Market Cap cut-off "31 July 2026", Indicative Review Products circulated "21 August 2026", Query Period "21 August 2026 to 4 September 2026", Lock-Down Period (open of) "7 September 2026", Russell US Style Capping Cut-Off Date "9 September 2026", and REVIEW EFFECTIVE DATE (OPEN OF) "21 SEPTEMBER 2026". The same table's June 2026 column reproduces FTSE Russell's own published June schedule (lock-down 8 June 2026, effective open 29 June 2026 after the 26 June implementation), which is the internal check on the table's reliability. THE IMPLEMENTATION SESSION IS AN INFERENCE AND IS LABELLED AS ONE: the owner publishes the effective OPEN (2026-09-21, a Monday), and by the same open-of-the-following-Monday convention Appendix F of ground rules v7.2 states for reconstitution ("the day changes are made after the close of the market and become effective at the open on the Monday following"), the trade prints after the close of Friday 2026-09-18 -- which is the September quad-witching expiry already tracked here as opex-2026-09-18. Filed estimate for the same reason as every Russell entry in this calendar: the confirmed-tier source prefixes have no member for an index owner's own published schedule, and the FAQ table carries the owner's caveat "NOTE: Dates may be subject to change. Clients will be notified of any changes." Discovered during the russell-recon-lockdown-2026-11-30 initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED by the russell-recon-lockdown-2026-11-30 initial research (2026-09-06), which found it while reading the FTSE Russell FAQ's four-column 2026 schedule table for the December lock-down date. WHY IT IS WORTH A CALENDAR ENTRY: this calendar tracks five Russell entries and every one of them is a semi-annual reconstitution milestone; the QUARTERLY leg is untracked entirely, and it is the nearest Russell flow date on the board -- 15 days out, against 85 for the December lock-down and 274 for the June 2027 one. It is also the only Russell date in this chain whose implementation collides with an expiry: the flow prints into the opex-2026-09-18 quad-witching close, which is a genuine execution-hygiene fact rather than a directional claim. THE SCOPE IS SMALL AND IS STATED UP FRONT so nobody sizes it as a reconstitution: the quarterly review adds only IPOs from the 1 May to 31 July 2026 review period, with no cap-tier migration, no style re-scoring of the universe and no float re-weighting -- the owner's own November 2025 parallel-run paper puts even the DECEMBER leg's R2000 turnover at 5.37% against June's 10.43%, and a quarterly IPO leg is far smaller again. Impact low and symbols deliberately EMPTY, for the same reason as its siblings: the flow is in the individual names entering, an ETF proxy would make the deterministic screen trip on small-cap beta, and no house playbook is index-flow-keyed. A SECOND FINDING TRAVELS WITH THIS PROPOSAL and is the reason the id is worth having on the board at all: this quarterly leg's own lock-down date, owner-published as 7 September 2026, IS LABOR DAY, a full US market holiday -- which establishes that FTSE Russell's "Lock-Down Period (open of)" is an index-administration boundary and not a trading-session one, correcting the reading in the russell-recon-lockdown-2027-06-07 ledger that treated ground-rules 6.4.1's "from the open" as a session boundary. Kind sector matches the sibling market-structure flow entries; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named, not fixed from this lane. ONE DATED MILESTONE WAS DELIBERATELY NOT PROPOSED, and the reasoning is recorded so a later lane does not re-litigate it: the FAQ also publishes a "Russell US Style Capping Cut-Off Date" of 2 December 2026, inside the December lock-down window, but nothing publishes on it, no shares move on it and it is a data cut-off for a leg the owner has already said is reduced in December -- the same class of non-event the russell-recon-preliminary-2026-11-13 lane declined.
